question: Should OpenClaw core accept this opt-in continuation subsystem with trusted cross-session delegate-return delivery in this PR, or require a narrower RFC/API-security split first?
rationale: The diff changes model tools, config defaults, persisted session/task state, gateway protocol internals, and trusted cross-session context delivery, so the product and security boundary cannot be settled by code review alone.

options.title: Approve behind proof gates
options.body: Keep the broad feature scope only after explicit approval of trusted cross-session delivery and exact-head proof for enabled, fresh-install, upgrade, and high-context request_compaction paths.

options.title: Split the subsystem
options.body: Ask for a smaller continuation substrate PR and defer cross-session targeting, plugin/API exposure, docs, and broader integrations to separately reviewed follow-ups.

options.title: Pause core inclusion
options.body: Keep this experimental outside core if maintainers do not want a model-facing continuation primitive in OpenClaw now.

recommendation.title: Approve behind proof gates
recommendation.body: Keep the broad feature scope only after explicit approval of trusted cross-session delivery and exact-head proof for enabled, fresh-install, upgrade, and high-context request_compaction paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main ownership signal spans the affected agent, config, session, and system-event surfaces.
